sync_total 280 -> 282 (want an increase: the restarted process must reach the homeserver at all). initial_sync_total 1 -> 1 — an increase here means it re-seeded; no increase means it resumed a persisted cursor

the fixture answered 1 sync(s) after the restart; they carried [{"sync":281,"initial":false,"served":["$f240d3685degap"]}]; looking for $f240d3685degap -> true (on a incremental sync). THIS IS THE H2 EXCLUSION: without it a zero below could mean the fixture never served the message, which is a harness fault and not product loss. where=incremental means the adapter resumed and ASKED for the window it missed; where=initial means it was offered the window on a sync whose timeline it discards
arrivals=1 want=1 — a message sent AFTER the restart. Without this, a process that came up broken would look identical to one that dropped only the gap

verdict=PASS arrivals=1 want>=1 for a message delivered to the homeserver while the binary was down and served back to the restarted process. CONTROLS HELD: pre-restart delivery=1, post-restart delivery=1, fixture served the event after the restart=true (on a incremental sync). A zero here is silent inbound loss across a restart: the cursor did not survive the process, so the first /sync after the restart was an initial sync whose timeline the replay guard discards — exactly the window that was missed.
